subject: [Urgent] Medigrid p95 spike on omega-xr v2.4 — emergency rollback decision
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: medigrid p95 spike observed on omega-xr v2.4

Markus / Ben —

Monitoring fired for Medigrid's production tenant at 08:47 UTC. p95 for text-generation requests using model omega-xr v2.4 jumped from 230ms to 1.4s for long-context workflows (>2k tokens). Error rate is stable; throughput unchanged. This looks like a KV-cache eviction pattern tied to the new quantized kernels we rolled last night.

Quick summary:
- Affected variants: omega-xr v2.4 (quantized 4-bit path) serving long-context routes only
- Impact: p95 up ~1.1s, p99 up ~2.8s for ~18% of traffic from Medigrid (long prompt batch)
- Time window: spike began 2028-04-13T08:45:00Z, intermittent since then

I attached a short CSV with sampled requests and a diag snapshot. Recommend immediate rollback to v2.3 for Medigrid or traffic pin to classic-omega (non-quant) while we investigate. Medigrid is on enterprise SLA; Tom is already on standby (he's copied below).

Asking for authorization to execute emergency rollback for Medigrid only (canary rollback) — this will take ~12-15 minutes with a short scheduling window. If approved, I'll trigger the runbook and notify Ops and the customer.

-Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
ops@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-13T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: medigrid p95 spike observed on omega-xr v2.4

Markus —

Thanks for the heads up. I just spoke with Tom at Medigrid, he's reporting elevated latencies in the production app and is worried about hitting their consumer-facing SLO. They asked if we can avoid a full rollback (they prefer a targeted route pin to keep new capabilities live), but they're open to a temporary rollback if it reduces risk.

Customer ask: keep the model capability stable for short user flows, rollback for long-context worker routes.

From a commercial perspective, we should move fast — if we breach p95 SLA for Medigrid we'll need to negotiate credits and it could hurt renewal conversations. Authorize whatever gets latency stabilized fastest.

-Ben

--
Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-13T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: medigrid p95 spike observed on omega-xr v2.4

Thanks — I need a short decision path. Per the SLA carveout policy, product/ops can authorize a customer-scoped rollback for service-stability reasons, but I need explicit sign-off from CS/sales for customer-facing tradeoffs. Ben, you just gave the commercial preference. Neha / leadership: can you sign off on a targeted rollback now (Medigrid only) while we triage the quantized kernel interaction?

Operational note: the rollback runbook is attached — can be completed with zero config changes to customer app and will preserve traffic for other customers on v2.4. If we need an emergency-wide rollback, that's a different approval path.

Proposed action (vote):
1) Authorize targeted rollback to omega-xr v2.3 for Medigrid long-context routes now (expected 15m)
2) Open postmortem and suspend further 4-bit kernel rollouts until triage complete

Please reply with APPROVE / REJECT and include any alternate suggestions.

-Markus

--
Markus Klein
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-13T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: medigrid p95 spike observed on omega-xr v2.4

APPROVE.

Given Medigrid's contract (enterprise, committed throughput) and the clear customer impact, authorize the targeted rollback for the affected routes. Please ensure Ops notifies the customer with a short note that we're reverting a recent model performance change to stabilize latency and that we will follow up with a postmortem and timeline for a safe re-roll.

Also: include the risk note for potential transient cache-warmup latency after rollback — communicate that to Tom.

-Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@medigrid.com>
Date: 2028-04-13T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: ACTION: executing targeted rollback for Medigrid now (omega-xr v2.4 -> v2.3)

Markus / Ben —

Rolling back Medigrid long-context routes to omega-xr v2.3 at 10:20 UTC. ETA ~15 minutes. Tom — we'll post a short note in the next 30m with the action and what to expect (brief warmup latency). We'll also open a ticket and keep you updated in-channel.

Attachments: runbook-omega-xr-rollback.pdf, medigrid-p95-samples-20280413.csv, diag-snapshot-omega-xr.png

I'll follow up with a stabilization check (p95/p99) and then confirm post-rollback state.

-Hannah

Date: 2028-04-15T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACTION: executing targeted rollback for Medigrid now (omega-xr v2.4 -> v2.3)

Thanks for the prompt response and the rollback. We observed the p95 reduce back into expected ranges within ~20 minutes; the app logged a couple of slow warmup traces but overall things look good. Appreciate the targeted approach — keeps the new capabilities intact for other customers while stabilizing our workload.

We'll expect the postmortem and timeline for a safe re-roll when available.

-Tom
